memories.text: I live in Accra for now, out in East Legon, and the traffic on the motorway eats two hours a day.
I keep the core network running at Volta Telecom, and outages always happen at 3am.
I'm a network engineer, routers and fibre are my whole world.
Highlife is my music, and I grew up dancing to it at every family party.
Please include links to sources when you tell me facts, I like to check.
People keep asking, but I'm not allergic to fish, I just don't like tilapia bones.
My sister Akosua lives in Tamale and runs every family group chat.
Our network change window is on Friday nights, which kills my weekends.
Router rollout: back up the config, push the firmware at 2am, verify BGP sessions, and roll back if packet loss goes above one percent.
I volunteer on Sunrise, a project building solar mini-grids for villages.
Sunrise is still in the site survey phase, lots of driving on dirt roads.
I joined the Labadi Football Club veterans team, we play on the beach on Saturdays.
Went on safari at Mole National Park and an elephant walked right past the jeep.
I'm allergic to aspirin, so I always tell pharmacists before they hand me anything.
For kenkey I soak the maize for three days, grind it, ferment the dough, and steam it wrapped in plantain leaves.
Correction: the change window moved to Sunday nights, traffic is lower then.
My nephew's naming ceremony will be in Ho next month.
Sunrise is owned by the Northern Electrification Trust, which pays for the panels.
Sunrise got delayed by the rainy season, the trucks couldn't reach the sites.
Went to Afrochella with my cousins and danced until sunrise.
Change of plan, the naming ceremony moved to Tema because grandma can't travel far.
We've got a little goat in the yard that eats everything, including my shoes.
I don't drink coffee at all, it makes my heart race.
Remind me to renew my passport before the end of February.
I moved to Kumasi in April, and the markets here are on another level.
Since April I've been with Ashanti Solar, running their monitoring network.
Ashanti Solar has its headquarters in Takoradi, close to the harbour.
My manager is Efua Mensah, she's an absolute legend in the energy sector.
Efua lives in Cape Coast and visits the Kumasi office twice a month.
I enrolled in a CCNP certification course, lots of late-night lab work ahead.
These days amapiano is all I play, my old playlists are gathering dust.
Sunrise is now powering 40 households, the kids can do homework at night.
Spent Christmas in Lagos with friends and survived the traffic.
I earned the CCNP certification on my first attempt.
Commissioning a mini-grid: check battery voltage, test the inverter under load, and get sign-off from the village committee.
I've never been to Asia, but I'd love to see Singapore.
I like my jollof with extra pepper, the hotter the better.
Remind me to pay the football club fees before the 1st of August.
